interface_detail: [translated] Signup and scaling are through signup.kagoya.jp; the page documents immediate scale-up and annual payment.
chaining: A USD 3.5 per month Japanese root guest is the fallback if no free Asian endpoint survives; it also measures whether an address in Japan is what a target wants.
binding_note: Nothing in the free sense binds because there is no free tier. At 1 TiB/month the binding factor is the price: a 1 GB plan at a 550 yen monthly cap is cheap but not zero, and no traffic allowance is published to fail first.

identity_cost.detail: Signup is at signup.kagoya.jp. The pages read do not state what a new account must supply; the card or email requirement is not established here.

reliability_note: Daily billing means a machine can be created for one day; nothing on the page suggests a reclamation risk on a paid plan.
confidence_note: The daily rate and monthly cap are vendor sentences with a date. A Japanese comparison site claims a 14-day free trial for KAGOYA; the vendor page read does not mention one, so it is not recorded.

evidence.proved: [translated] '1 GB: 20 yen per day, monthly cap 550 yen', and 'all plans have no initial cost', billed per day, month or year.
